items.s: The University of Sydney ____ the findings on 21 October 2026.

tfn.s: The research was announced by the University of Sydney.
tfn.why: The text says: "The University of Sydney announced the findings on 21 October 2026."

tfn.s: Depression is simply a problem of going to bed too late.
tfn.why: The text says: "This does not mean that depression is simply a problem of going to bed too late."

tfn.s: Most of the people in the group were teenagers.
tfn.why: The text does not say how old the people in the group were.

tfn.s: If a medicine is not working, people should talk to a doctor.
tfn.why: The text says: "If a medicine is not working, the safest step is to talk to a qualified doctor rather than stop taking it."

tfn.s: The study tested treatments for the body clock.
tfn.why: The text says: "This study did not test those treatments."

focus.note: A collocation is a pair of words that always go together. Learn the pair, not just the word.

tfn.s: The study included more than 10,000 Australians.
tfn.why: The text says: "analysed clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians who had experienced depression"

tfn.s: The 2,604 participants represent everyone with depression.
tfn.why: The text says: "so the percentage should not be taken as a figure for everyone who experiences low mood or depression"

tfn.s: All of the participants lived in Sydney.
tfn.why: The text does not say where in Australia the participants lived.

tfn.s: The study shows that light therapy works for people with circadian depression.
tfn.why: The text says the researchers suggested such treatments might deserve attention, "although this study did not test them".

tfn.s: People should change their medication if an article suggests it.

focus.note: Many collocations are verb + noun or adjective + noun. Say the whole chunk aloud so it sounds natural.

tfn.s: The study can say little about how a person's symptoms change over time.
tfn.why: The data were "gathered at a single point in time", so changes over time cannot be shown.

tfn.s: The authors recommend that patients with this profile switch to light therapy.
tfn.why: The text says the treatments "are not blanket recommendations" and that the study "did not test those treatments".

tfn.s: The independent expert criticised the researchers for relying on what patients reported about their treatment.
tfn.why: The text says only that an independent expert called the work exploratory.

tfn.s: Recognising the subtype could one day reduce trial-and-error prescribing.
tfn.why: The text says it "could eventually help clinicians move beyond a trial-and-error approach".

tfn.s: Anyone who stays up late by choice can be assumed to have circadian depression.

speak.title: Role-play: should I stop my medicine?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your patient has read a news story about body clocks and wants to stop their medicine. Ask about their sleep and how they feel. Explain why they shouldn't change anything without advice.

b.text: You read a story about body clocks and depression. You're worried your medicine isn't working. Explain why you want to stop, and ask the doctor what you can do instead.

phrases: I read a story about body clocks.
I'm thinking of stopping my medicine.
I'd like to understand why it isn't working.
That's an early study, so please don't stop yet.
Let's talk about your sleep first.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the patient decide to keep the medicine, and why?
